description:
## CONTEXT

Lens selection is extension/path based and content-blind, the activation list has no disclosure of what was skipped, there is no way to define a repo-specific lens, and cached findings replay across commits without re-validation. From the 2026-07-03 dynamic-selection review and field report plus codex rulings 1, 5, and 8 (decision record: workspace N-076). The pen edge (vectors no fixed set anticipates) needs a caller-supplied custom-lens slot riding the same pipeline; the floor needs a conservative always-run baseline with disclosed skips.

## VERIFIED STATE @ a9f49dd

- `activate()` receives only path strings: `activate({stage, changedFiles, config})` (src/lenses/registry.ts:295-299); `start.ts` passes only `changedFiles` even though the artifact/diff is in hand (start.ts:162-166). `matchesSurface` checks extension/segment/basename only (registry.ts:209-223). Selection is content-blind.
- Skips are invisible on the wire: `activate()` drops non-matching lenses with `if (activationReason === null) continue` (registry.ts:340) and `maxLenses` truncation is a plain declaration-order slice (registry.ts:350-355). `StartToolOutputSchema` carries only `reviewId`, `agents[]`, `cached[]` (start.ts:87-109) -- no skipped list, no `activationReason` (it is computed at registry.ts:342-347 but only lands inside the prompt text via prompt-builder.ts:94-96).
- `maxLenses` truncation can drop a core lens: declaration order is security, error-handling, clean-code, performance, api-design, concurrency, test-quality, accessibility; the slice at registry.ts:350-355 keeps performance/api-design (surface) and can drop concurrency, which is a `"core"` lens per SURFACE_RULES (registry.ts:130-134). The docstring (registry.ts:284-289) claims truncation keeps core lenses, but the implementation does not partition.
- Project-local lenses are impossible: `LENS_IDS` is a compile-time array from `LENSES` (registry.ts:19), `LensIdSchema` is a closed `z.enum` (registry.ts:20), the allow-list is `z.array(LensIdSchema)` (registry.ts:57-61), and the wire output `agents[].id` is `LensIdSchema` (start.ts:93). A project-defined id cannot pass validation. Precedent for a trust posture: caller-supplied `projectRules` is wrapped in `<untrusted-context>` (shared-preamble.ts:169-173).
- Cache replays with no re-validation: `readLensCache` keys on the prompt hash; a hit returns cached findings wholesale (start.ts:183-189). Lenses are instructed to Read/Grep beyond the diff (security.ts:145; test-quality.ts:80) and that repo state is not in the hash, so a cached finding derived from since-changed surrounding code replays within the 24h TTL.

## SCOPE

1. Content-aware classification atop SURFACE_RULES: `activate()` may consult caller-supplied signals (a DiffProfile: languages, per-file class, size, added-line risk markers for auth/SQL/concurrency/fs-writes/network/secrets). Markers only ADD lenses to a conservative always-run baseline; they never remove lenses. An explicit `config.lenses` allow-list still overrides. The signals are COMPUTED BY THE CONSUMER (the party with filesystem access) and passed in -- see workspace WF1 (ID assigned later) for the prepare-side half. This ticket accepts the signals and maps them, keeping `activate()` pure (codex ruling 5; ruling 7 typed context).
2. Partition `maxLenses`: always retain the full core set and trim only surface lenses (fix registry.ts:350-355 to `[...core, ...surface.slice(0, maxLenses - core.length)]`); reject `maxLenses` below the core count at the schema, or exempt core from the cap.
3. Per-lens status disclosure on the wire: add a `decisions` array to `StartToolOutput` (start.ts:87-109) with one entry per known lens -- `{id, decision: spawned|cached|skipped, reason, matchedSignals[]}`. Absence of a finding must never read as success (codex ruling 6).
4. Caller force-include/exclude with reasons: config gains explicit include/exclude lists the caller annotates; both are disclosed in the `decisions` array.
5. Custom lens input (codex ruling 1): accept a caller-supplied `projectLenses` param. Split `LensIdSchema` into a closed `BuiltinLensIdSchema` | a `ProjectLensIdSchema` regex `^custom:[a-z0-9-]+/[a-z0-9-]+$`. The server force-namespaces ids to `custom:<caller>/<id>`, REJECTS any slug colliding with a built-in id, records `promptHash` + provenance in the envelope, never lets a custom lens shadow a built-in's policy tables, and NORMALIZES caller-suggested severity (callers suggest; the server clamps to the declared `maxSeverity`; blocking status is never caller-set). The custom lens body renders AFTER the server-owned preamble so it can bind domain rules but can never redefine the Safety section or the output JSON contract; escape any literal `</untrusted-context>` sequence in the body.
6. Project-local definitions discovered by the CONSUMER (workspace WF1) and passed in as custom lenses -- e.g. an RLS-binding lens carrying its tenancy rules and known-bitten file list. This ticket only defines the server-side custom-lens contract; discovery of `.story/lenses/` is WF1's half.
7. Cache safety: re-validate cache hits against the current artifact (requires LF1's retention + evidence anchoring) so a cached finding is surfaced only if its evidence still verifies; OR include a caller-supplied repo-state fingerprint (e.g. HEAD sha) in the cache key so cross-commit replay never happens silently.
8. Deterministic risk-template middle tier (codex ruling 8): a server-side library of parameterized narrow vectors (migrations, concurrency, fs-writes) so targeted coverage does not require a bespoke pen-authored prompt.

## OUT OF SCOPE

The consumer-side prepare that computes the DiffProfile and discovers `.story/lenses/` definitions (workspace WF1); the retention mechanism (LF1). Cache-revalidation-by-evidence depends on LF1; the repo-state-fingerprint fallback ships without it.

## ACCEPTANCE

- Test: `maxLenses: 5` on an `/api/` diff keeps all four core lenses and trims a surface lens (concurrency survives; api-design is trimmed).
- Test: `StartToolOutput.decisions` has one entry per known lens with a reason; a skipped lens is visible with its reason.
- Test: a custom lens `custom:acme/rls-binding` passes wire validation, cannot be named to collide with a built-in, and its caller-suggested "blocking" severity is normalized down.
- Test: a cache hit whose repo-state fingerprint differs from the current one is NOT replayed silently (either re-validated or treated as a miss).
- Test: added-line risk markers ADD a lens to the baseline but never remove one; the always-run baseline is present on every CODE_REVIEW.
- Test: a custom lens body containing a `</untrusted-context>` sequence is escaped and cannot break out of its block.

## PITFALLS

- The closed-enum change (registry.ts:19-20) is load-bearing; splitting `LensIdSchema` touches every wire boundary that references it (start.ts:93,104; `LensConfigSchema` at registry.ts:57-63) -- change them together.
- Custom lenses are UNTRUSTED for behavior but caller-trusted for configuration; they must never redefine the Safety or output contract (codex ruling 2). Render order matters.
- Content markers must scan ADDED diff lines, not whole files, to avoid pre-existing code flipping lenses -- but the added-line extraction is the consumer's job (WF1); this ticket consumes the signals, so validate them defensively.
- Do not let selection changes desync the "core lens" set that LF2's coverage rule reads -- keep a single source in the registry.
- Cache re-validation that depends on LF1 must degrade gracefully (fingerprint fallback) if LF1 has not landed.

## VERIFICATION

Run activation fixtures for (a) `maxLenses` core-retention, (b) `decisions` completeness, (c) a custom-lens round-trip with severity normalization and namespace-collision rejection, and (d) a cross-commit cache replay blocked by fingerprint mismatch; confirm the always-run baseline fires on an empty-marker diff.

## SIZING

XL. registry.ts (enum split, partitioned truncation, content-aware map, risk templates), start.ts (decisions output, `projectLenses` param), schema (LensId split, custom-lens schema), cache/lens-cache.ts (fingerprint/re-validation), shared-preamble/prompt-builder (custom-lens render). The largest of the seven; split into child tickets during planning. Portable enough for the lowest permitted execution tier per child ticket once decomposed.

Cross-link: workspace N-076. The project-local discovery half is workspace WF1 (ID assigned later). Cache-revalidation soft-depends on LF1.

## PLAN-REVIEW RULINGS (2026-07-04, wave 3b, binding):

The wave-3 plan gate ran two rounds (plan + revision) against HEAD 770cfd5. Round 1 produced 11 findings; the revised plan resolved all 11 and the round-2 reviewers verified those resolutions as factually correct against source. Round 2 produced 9 new findings, which parked the item. Every disputed fact below was re-verified in source at 770cfd5. Rulings R1-R9 resolve the round-2 findings; R10-R18 ratify the round-1 resolutions as binding so a fresh plan does not regress them. All line numbers cited are at 770cfd5; anchor edits by symbol, not line.

R1 (round-2 codex 1, expected-lens gate in complete.ts; BLOCKING). ADOPTED. `lens_review_complete` must enforce that submitted lens ids are a subset of the session's `expectedLensIds`. Verified: complete.ts:327 accepts any `r.lensId in LENSES` even if never activated, excluded, or dropped by an allow-list; applyCompletion checks only MISSING expected lenses (review-state.ts:461,487), never extras; `let session` (complete.ts:302) is assigned only after applyCompletion (:411), so the gate cannot read `session`. Required behavior: load `const preSession = getReview(parsed.reviewId)` (exported at review-state.ts:306) BEFORE the first-pass loop (the same preSession R12's custom-lens gate needs); classify any `r.lensId` not in `preSession.expectedLensIds` as an internal parseError (phase "internal", message naming the unexpected id) and `continue` without entering `submissions`; ALSO enforce the subset invariant inside applyCompletion so the state machine owns it. Custom/template ids are in expectedLensIds by construction (R8), so they pass this gate naturally. When preSession is undefined (unknown reviewId), do NOT classify anything; fall through so applyCompletion's unknown-reviewId rejection surfaces exactly as today. Mandated test: start with an exclude (or allow-list) that drops a built-in lens, submit a result for that lens, assert it lands in parseErrors and its findings never reach perLens or the verdict.

R2 (round-2 codex 2, template ids accepted before templates exist). ADOPTED as an invariant over commit ordering: at NO commit in the sequence may `LensConfigSchema.lenses` accept a `template:` id while an allow-listed `template:` id with no matching implementation silently produces zero activation. Satisfy it either way: (a) delay adding TemplateLensIdSchema to the `config.lenses` union until the risk-template work package, or (b) if the union widens earlier, that SAME commit implements the missing-definition isError path for `template:` ids (message naming the id, mirroring the `custom:` rule in R8). A test pinning the isError (or the deferred schema) lands in whichever commit widens the schema.

R3 (round-2 codex 3, unbounded caller strings). ADOPTED with exact caps: include/exclude `reason` z.string().min(1).max(512); `diffProfile.languages` entries max 64 chars each (array cap 32); `diffProfile.files[].path` max 1024 chars (array cap 512); riskTemplates `params.paths` entries max 1024 chars each (array cap 32); `params.notes` max 2048; projectLenses `body` max 16384. Rule: every caller string echoed into decisions[]/matchedSignals or persisted must be either a closed enum or explicitly length-capped at the schema.

R4 (round-2 codex 4, duplicate ids within include/exclude). ADOPTED. The include/exclude superRefine must reject, naming the offending id in the validation issue: (a) the same id present in both lists, (b) duplicate ids within include, (c) duplicate ids within exclude, in addition to rejecting array-form `lenses` combined with include/exclude.

R5 (round-2 byte 1, partition vs explicit allow-list; BLOCKING). ADOPTED per the reviewer's recommendation: maxLenses core/include protection applies ONLY to organic activations. When array-form `config.lenses` is set, retain today's plain slice semantics: the caller's cap wins and may trim any lens, cores included. Verified: test/lens-registry-activate.test.ts:428-438 pins lenses [security, error-handling, clean-code, performance] + maxLenses 2 -> [security, error-handling]; that test must remain green UNCHANGED. This is consistent with the precedence chain (allow-list outranks everything; registry.ts:334 already skips unlisted cores today) and with R10. Conflict resolution vs R11: no conflict is reachable because the schema makes array-form `lenses` mutually exclusive with include/exclude, so include-protection never meets an allow-list. Any test-audit range a plan cites for existing maxLenses tests MUST include lines 428-438, not just 396-425. Mandated tests: the existing 428-438 pin stays byte-identical; a new organic-path (no allow-list) test pins core survival under the cap.

R6 (round-2 byte 2, PLAN_REVIEW maxLenses semantics; BLOCKING). RULING: core-protection does NOT apply at PLAN_REVIEW. "Core" is a SURFACE_RULES concept (registry.ts:146-149) scoped to CODE_REVIEW; on PLAN_REVIEW all lenses activate with reason "plan review: all lenses" and the cap keeps today's declaration-order slice. Rationale (conservative, repo-derived): the existing test test/lens-registry-activate.test.ts:396-403 (maxLenses 3 on PLAN_REVIEW -> [security, error-handling, clean-code]) pins current wire behavior for existing PLAN_REVIEW callers; protecting cores there would be a wire-visible cap overrun. That test must remain green UNCHANGED. The protected set is therefore stage-dependent: CODE_REVIEW -> CORE_LENS_IDS union include ids; PLAN_REVIEW -> include ids only; either stage with array-form allow-list -> empty (R5). The activate() docstring must state this stage scoping explicitly. Mandated test: one dedicated PLAN_REVIEW cap test pinning the chosen semantics (existing 396-403 stays, plus one PLAN_REVIEW cap-with-include fixture).

R7 (round-2 byte 3, third filename interpolation site in lens-cache). ADOPTED. `fileSafeLensId` (colon/slash -> "_") must cover ALL sites that interpolate lensId into a path: src/cache/lens-cache.ts `lensCacheFilePath` (:138), writeLensCache's inline `final` (join at :209), the tmp nonce path (:222-225), and src/cache/in-flight.ts `promptPath`/`taskPath` (:174-189). Preferred implementation: refactor writeLensCache so both `final` and `tmp` route through fileSafeLensId/lensCacheFilePath, leaving zero inline lensId interpolations. Failure mode being foreclosed: a `custom:acme/x` id embeds "/" in the filename, writeFileSync throws ENOENT, persistLensCacheBestEffort's best-effort catch swallows it, and cache writes fail silently while reads permanently miss. Mandated test: writeLensCache with a `custom:` id followed by readLensCache round-trips through the real files, plus fileSafeLensId unit tests (colon/slash mapping, built-in ids unchanged, injectivity given [a-z0-9-] slugs).

R8 (round-1 codex 3 + round-1 byte 2, allow-list interaction with custom/template lenses). RATIFIED as specified in the revised plan: ONE rule spans built-ins, projectLenses, and riskTemplates. When `config.lenses` is the array form it filters the ENTIRE activation universe by wire id: a supplied custom/template item whose wire id is not named gets a decisions entry skipped with reason exactly "not in allow-list", is not spawned, and is EXCLUDED from expectedLensIds. An allow-list entry naming a `custom:`/`template:` id with NO matching supplied definition is an isError response (the caller's config contradicts itself; silent proceed would weaken the explicit contract). `lenses: "auto"` and absent behave as today (all supplied customs/templates activate). Mandated three-arm test: (a) allow-list without the custom id -> skipped + excluded from expectedLensIds; (b) allow-list naming both a built-in and the custom id -> both spawn; (c) allow-list naming a custom id with no definition -> isError. Same arms for templates (R2).

R9 (round-2 byte 5, include/exclude stage scoping and plan-kind rank). ADOPTED per the reviewer's simplest resolution: include/exclude apply at BOTH stages, and include OUTRANKS the T-030 plan-kind exclusion (PLAN_KIND_EXCLUSIONS, registry.ts:88-92): an included accessibility spawns on planKind backend/infra with the caller-include reason. Repo precedent: at HEAD the explicit allow-list already bypasses the plan-kind filter (registry.ts:334-340 sets "explicit lens allow-list" before the plan-kind branch is consulted), so caller-explicit selection outranking the plan-kind hint introduces no new capability class. Full precedence chain, to be stated verbatim in the plan and docstring: allow-list (mutually exclusive with include/exclude) > exclude > include > plan-kind exclusion > risk markers (CODE_REVIEW only) > surface/core (CODE_REVIEW) or all-lenses (PLAN_REVIEW). Mandated tests: one PLAN_REVIEW exclude fixture (lens skipped with the caller-exclude reason), one include-vs-planKind fixture (accessibility + planKind backend -> spawned with caller-include reason).

R10 (round-1 byte 3, exclude vs core baseline). RATIFIED: caller `exclude` MAY remove a core lens. This is deliberate and consistent with existing behavior (the array-form allow-list already drops cores today via registry.ts:334). The ACCEPTANCE bullet "the always-run baseline is present on every CODE_REVIEW" is hereby AMENDED to read: the core baseline (CORE_LENS_IDS) fires on every CODE_REVIEW absent caller allow-list/exclude overrides; risk markers and the maxLenses cap never remove it. Mandated test: exclude security on CODE_REVIEW -> security decision skipped with reason "caller exclude: <reason>"; the other three core lenses remain.

R11 (round-1 codex 2, includes protected from the cap). RATIFIED: caller include entries join the protected set for maxLenses partitioning (stage-dependent per R6; void under an allow-list per R5). An included lens can never be trimmed by maxLenses; its decisions entry shows the caller-include reason, never the trim reason. If maxLenses is below the protected activation count, the kept set degrades to the protected activations only (schema keeps .min(1); no breaking wire change). Mandated test: include accessibility + maxLenses 5 on a surface-heavy diff -> accessibility survives, the trim falls on unprotected surface lenses.

R12 (round-1 byte 1, complete.ts data flow and clamp placement). RATIFIED: `getReview(parsed.reviewId)` is called BEFORE the first-pass loop; undefined preSession means an empty customLenses map and no early misclassification ahead of applyCompletion's unknown-reviewId rejection. The custom/template severity clamp is applied to the parsed output IMMEDIATELY after a successful LensOutputSchema.safeParse, BEFORE pushing into `submissions`, so perLensLatestOutput, on-disk task records (persistInFlightBestEffort reads `submissions`), the merger verdict, and hop-2 cache writeback ALL see clamped severities. A clamp placed at perLens assembly or on the wire verdict is FORBIDDEN (it would persist unclamped caller-set blocking severities to disk). Verified: session-out-of-scope-during-loop at complete.ts:302/:327/:411.

R13 (round-1 codex 5, cached custom results bypassing the ceiling). RATIFIED, both directions: (1) the declared maxSeverity is rendered into the server-owned section of the custom/template prompt, so it enters the SHA-256 prompt hash by construction; the same body under a different ceiling produces a different promptHash and can never replay across a ceiling change; (2) belt-and-suspenders clamp-on-read: cache hits for custom/template lenses are clamped to the declared ceiling BEFORE entering cachedResults/cachedWire, so even a hand-forged or legacy cache file at the current hash cannot surface an over-ceiling severity. Mandated tests: cache with maxSeverity major then rerun the byte-identical body with minor -> spawned (different hash), not cached; hand-write an over-ceiling record at the current hash -> surfaced clamped.

R14 (round-1 codex 1 + round-1 byte 5, WireLensId widening completeness). RATIFIED: the id widening ships COMPLETE in one commit so no unsafe casts survive on the retry/cache/merger paths, covering: prompt-builder.ts `AgentPrompt.lensId` (pinned `readonly lensId: LensId` at :59 today), pipeline.ts `LensRunResult.lensId`, complete.ts `RetryCandidate.lensId` / `agentSubmittedLensIds` / persistLensCacheBestEffort's set param, review-state.ts session maps + expectedLensIds + SubmittedResult + registerReview params + hydrateFromDisk casts (`as LensId` -> `as WireLensId`), start.ts local containers, lens-cache.ts `CachedLensResultSchema.lensId` + function params, and get-prompt.ts replacing the `as never` cast (:88) with `as WireLensId`. PINNED: get-prompt does NOT parse lensId through WireLensIdSchema (GetPromptParamsSchema.lensId stays z.string().min(1)); a Map.get on a non-member string returns undefined and yields the identical not-found error, avoiding a wire-behavior change. Custom/template agents MUST flow through the existing spawnedAgents loop that populates the lensModels map handed to registerReview, because persistRegistrationBestEffort skips lensMeta entries with undefined model (review-state.ts:233); otherwise custom promptHashes/perLensExpiresAt cannot rehydrate after restart. Mandated: restart-safety test (clear in-memory map, complete still clamps and rehydrates custom promptHash/expiry); `npx tsc --noEmit` gate before this commit. No merger edits beyond pipeline.ts are needed (see R15 for the correct citations).

R15 (round-2 byte 4, incorrect merger citation). CORRECTED, re-verified at 770cfd5: MergedFindingSchema has NO lensId field. The correct no-further-merger-edits justification is: `MergedFindingSchema.contributingLenses` is z.array(z.string().min(1)).nonempty() (src/schema/finding.ts:79); `DeferralKeySchema.lensId` is z.string().min(1) (src/schema/finding.ts:158); `ParseErrorSchema.lensId` and `NextActionSchema.lensId` are z.string().min(1) (src/schema/review-protocol.ts:48, :92); dedup's contributingLenses is already string-widened (src/merger/dedup.ts:79). The substantive conclusion stands: custom wire ids pass the verdict schemas unmodified. Any plan citing "MergedFindingSchema.lensId" is citing a nonexistent symbol and must use the above instead.

R16 (round-1 byte 4, V1 denylist coverage for new prompt surfaces). RATIFIED: all NEW server-authored prompt text (the project-lens server-owned section and every risk-template render) must contain no V1_DENYLIST token (test/lens-bodies.test.ts:107: critical, recommendedImpact, inputSource, sink, assumptions, requiresMoreContext, evidence, suggestedFix). Extract V1_DENYLIST into a shared test helper; lens-bodies.test.ts imports it unchanged; the project-lens test asserts renderProjectLensServerSection output is token-free; the risk-template test asserts every RISK_TEMPLATES render (with a token-free params fixture) is token-free. Authoring rule: severity sentences use blocking/major/minor/suggestion vocabulary only; use "verify"/"proof"/"confirm", never "evidence".

R17 (round-1 codex 4, maxLenses resource-cap scope). RATIFIED: maxLenses governs BUILT-IN activation only; supplied custom/template lenses are never trimmed by it. The resource bound on the added tiers is schema-level: projectLenses.max(8) and riskTemplates.max(3), worst-case total 9 + 8 + 3 = 20 agents, every one disclosed in decisions[]. Rationale: custom/template lenses are individually enumerated by the caller in the same request (deliberate spend, analogous to cap-exempt includes); silently trimming explicitly-requested work is the exact failure mode decisions[] exists to prevent. This scope must be stated in the LensConfigSchema comment, the activate() docstring, and the listTools description.

R18 (round-1 codex 6, unused title field). RATIFIED: ProjectLensSpecSchema ships WITHOUT a `title` field in this ticket. A future ticket may add it the moment something renders it, with the same untrusted handling as `body`.

Gate notes for the next planner: the round-2 byte reviewer confirmed the revised plan's architecture, WP ordering, cross-ticket fences (CORE_LENS_IDS as the single source T-027/LF2 reads, session-keyed clamp composing with T-028, LF1 fingerprint fallback), and all RED expectations against 770cfd5; the rejections were precision gaps, all closed by R1-R9 above. A conforming plan must carry every ruling verbatim into its work packages and test lists. Lens count at 770cfd5 is nine built-ins (data-safety exists; maxLenses schema max is 9); the VERIFIED STATE section above predates that and cites a9f49dd line numbers, so re-anchor by symbol.
title: Selection v2 -- content-aware activation, per-lens disclosure, caller overrides, project-local custom lenses, cache re-validation
